infra-context · generated 2026-10-19

Infra map: Bunkai

How Bunkai is built, run and deployed, and the non-functional budgets it holds. Built from the app repo ../upex-bunkai-tms (branch staging, head c0712e9, 67 migrations), its /qa testability page (cross-checked against code), live probes of the staging and production health endpoints, and the legacy markdown under .context/SRS/ and .context/infrastructure/, which was written against 12 migrations and is now partly stale. Paths are relative to the app repo unless noted.

Overview

Bunkai is a single Next.js 15 App Router application that is both the web UI and the REST API (/api/v1), backed by one hosted Supabase project (Postgres 17 + Supabase Auth). There is no separate backend service and no ORM: route handlers and React Server Components call Supabase through its JS SDK, and Postgres Row-Level Security is the authorization layer. It is deployed to Vercel as serverless functions plus static assets; staging and production are two Vercel deployments of the same repo.

Architecture

Pattern: a feature-organised modular monolith. app/ holds routes (pages and API), lib/ holds one folder per domain (pure logic + Supabase RPC calls), components/ holds UI per domain. Business rules live mostly in Postgres: 93 function definitions (143 security definer occurrences) and 10 triggers across the migrations, called from TypeScript through lib/supabase/rpc.ts.

Auth flow

  1. The login page asks for an email first; POST /api/v1/auth/check-email answers whether the account exists and is confirmed.
  2. Existing account: password step, Supabase signInWithPassword, session stored in the sb-<project-ref>-auth-token cookie.
  3. New account: POST /api/v1/auth/signup creates an unconfirmed user and Supabase emails a 6-8 digit OTP; POST /api/v1/auth/confirm verifies it (verifyOtp), sets the session and mints a PAT.
  4. Secondary paths: magic link (POST /api/v1/auth/magic-link, then /auth/callback exchanges the code) and OAuth (/auth/oauth/github|google issues a CSRF state cookie, PKCE round-trip, back to /auth/callback). Supabase auto-links identities that share an email.
  5. Headless: POST /api/v1/auth/signin returns the Supabase session AND a fresh PAT in one call; POST /api/v1/tokens mints more PATs from a cookie or Bearer caller.
  6. Every authenticated API call goes through withApiHandler → resolveIdentity: Bearer first, else cookie. Both collapse into one Principal whose db client runs as that user (for a PAT, via a 60-second HS256 JWT signed with SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET), so RLS is identical for both. The concrete request shapes land in Phase 3's backend section.

Database at architecture level

One store: Supabase-hosted Postgres 17, schema public, 31 tables (all with RLS enabled) defined in supabase/migrations/. No ORM; generated types live in lib/types/supabase.ts (bun run types:gen). Subsystems: tenancy (workspaces, members, invites), authoring (projects, modules, user stories, acceptance criteria, ATCs and their steps/assertions), execution (tests, runs and their steps, environments), defects (bugs), planning (milestones), notifications, imports, and cross-cutting (activity log, access tokens, idempotency keys, feature flags). Tables, columns, relationships and state machines belong to the business-data-context map (project-context mode data), still a placeholder. QA reaches the database through DBHub (dbhub.toml in this QA repo) with two QA roles that bypass RLS.

Security architecture

  • Authentication: Supabase Auth sessions (cookie) and Bunkai PATs. A PAT is stored as SHA-256 in access_token_secrets (a table QA roles cannot read), looked up by a 12-character indexed prefix; every failure is a uniform 401.
  • Authorization: Postgres RLS on every table, driven by auth.uid() and the bunkai_is_workspace_member family of helpers. On top, PAT scopes (atc:read, atc:write, run:execute, workspace:admin) are checked in the API layer; a cookie session holds all four. A PAT bound to workspace A cannot act on workspace B; workspace:admin is never a default and is refused at signin/confirm.
  • Secrets: lib/env.ts validates required variables with Zod at boot and is server-only; the service-role key never reaches the browser bundle.
  • Transport: TLS and HSTS come from Vercel (observed strict-transport-security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload). No application security headers are configured (see nfr-security).

Performance hooks

  • GIN indexes: atcs.tsv full-text search and tests.tags.
  • /api/openapi is force-static with cache-control: public, max-age=300, s-maxage=300.
  • /api/v1, /api/v1/me, /api/v1/health are force-dynamic.
  • The Monaco step editor loads through next/dynamic.
  • No application rate limiter: auth endpoints relay Supabase's own OTP limits as 429 rate_limited.

Internal surfaces outside the public API

No /admin, /internal, /webhook or /cron routes exist. The only background work is the Jira import worker (Vercel after()) and the Postgres triggers above.

ADRs

No test-architecture ADR was seeded in this phase: the QA repo has not settled auth-in-tests or a selector contract yet, so there is nothing to record as discovered. The app repo carries its own product ADRs (cookie/PAT coexistence ADR-0001, no global admin ADR-0005, workspace-bound tokens ADR-0006, rate-limit follow-up ADR-0007) cited by its code; they live in the app repo, not in .context/ADR/.

QA relevance

  • Highest-value surfaces: cross-tenant isolation (RLS), cookie/PAT parity on every /api/v1 route, PAT scope and workspace binding, the email-first login state machine, idempotent POSTs, the Jira import job.
  • Test environments need a Supabase project with the QA roles provisioned, a confirmed test account, and SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET set on the deployment (without it every Bearer call fails with 500).

Failures a test must account for

  • Email: signup and magic-link tests depend on a real mailbox and on Supabase's OTP rate limit (relayed as 429). Invites send NO email: the API returns the accept link once and the inviter shares it.
  • Jira: a 429 retries with exponential backoff (1, 2, 4, 8, 16 s, honouring Retry-After); bad credentials fail the whole job with jira_unauthorized; per-issue failures accumulate in the job's errors[]. Only one active import per project.
  • OAuth: needs a real provider consent screen; flag as manual setup, not scripted E2E.

Auth flow (the contract for test-framework-adaptation)

RequestBodyResponse
POST /api/v1/auth/check-email{ email }{ exists, confirmed }
POST /api/v1/auth/signup{ email, password } (password ≥ 8)202 { status: "pending_confirmation", email }, no session; 409 if the user exists; 429 on the Supabase OTP limit
POST /api/v1/auth/confirm{ email, token, pat_name?, pat_expires_in_days? }200 same shape as signin; 401 bad or expired code
POST /api/v1/auth/signin{ email, password, pat_name?, pat_scopes?, pat_expires_in_days? } (password ≥ 6, expiry ≤ 365 days)200 { user, session: { access_token, refresh_token, expires_at, token_type }, pat: { token, id, name, scopes, expires_at }, warning } and the session cookies; uniform 401
POST /api/v1/tokens{ name, scopes, workspace_id? } with a cookie or Bearer201 { id, token, scopes, warning }; the token is shown once
GET /api/v1/me-auth.source is cookie or bearer (with scopes)
  • Session: Supabase cookie sb-<project-ref>-auth-token, refreshed by middleware.ts on every request.
  • Token: Authorization: Bearer bk_pat_<prefix>.<secret>; default scopes atc:read, atc:write, run:execute.
  • A cookie and a PAT for the same user work at the same time; neither revokes the other.
  • Test account: the QA bot listed on /qa; its passwords live in Jira Epic BK-29, never in this repo.

Test IDs strategy

  • data-testid is the convention: 467 distinct static ids across 82 files, plus dynamic ids that append the entity id (ac-row-${id}, ac-edit-${id}).
  • Names are kebab-case <feature>-<element>[-<state>] (bug-form-submit, home-open-bugs-error, start-run-empty); at least one outlier uses snake case (notifications_retry).
  • The shadcn primitives in components/ui carry none: ids sit on the feature components that use them.
  • Login ids, as documented on /qa and present in the form: login-email, login-continue, login-password, login-signin, login-create, login-otp, login-verify, login-resend, login-magic-link-toggle.

Database infrastructure

Hosted Supabase Postgres 17; backups are Supabase platform defaults (plan unknown). The migrations README names ONE remote project as the migration target; whether staging and production use separate Supabase projects is not visible in code. QA connects through the Session Pooler (5432), never the transaction pooler (6543).

Monitoring and rollback

  • Error tracking, uptime monitoring, APM: none. Only Vercel's stdout logs (structured JSON for API calls).
  • Rollback: no procedure in the repo. Vercel's own redeploy or promote of an earlier deployment is the only mechanism available.

QA relevance

  • Run tests against staging; production is read-only for QA.
  • Probe before a run: curl -s https://staging-upexbunkai.vercel.app/api/v1/health must return "env":"staging".
  • Never hardcode another preview URL: it would also report staging.

CI/CD

CI

None. The app repo has no .github/workflows, GitLab, CircleCI, Azure or Jenkins config. Quality gates are local git hooks only:

HookRuns
pre-commitbunx lint-staged, bun run types:check, bun run vars:check, bun run skills:check, and skills:registry:check when skill files are staged
pre-pushbun run format:check && bun run lint:check && bun run vars:env:check && bun run skills:registry:check

No hook and no pipeline runs the 126 unit and isolation tests (bun test) or next build; hooks can be skipped with --no-verify.

Deployment

ItemValue
PlatformVercel, framework preset (no vercel.json, no Dockerfile)
Buildnext build
TriggerVercel Git integration on push (inferred from two live deployments and no other deploy config)
Database changesOut of band: migrations are applied by a developer through the Supabase MCP, not by the deploy
IaCNot present

Deployment checklist (what exists today)

  • Pre-deploy: local hooks; migrations applied to Supabase before or after the push by hand.
  • Post-deploy: GET /api/v1/health reports the environment name.
  • Rollback: Vercel dashboard or CLI (redeploy an earlier deployment); database migrations have no down scripts.

QA relevance

  • Nothing gates a merge on tests, so this QA repo's regression run is the first automated test signal a deploy gets.
  • A schema change can reach staging before or after the code that needs it: when a staging failure looks like a missing column or function, check the migration state first.
  • A CI job for this QA repo can trigger on a Vercel deploy and gate on the health probe.

Discovery gaps

  • Branch to environment mapping: staging → staging and main → production is inferred from branch names and the Vercel preview mapping; the Vercel project settings are not in the repo. Confirm with the dev team.
  • One Supabase project or two: the migrations README names a single remote project; whether staging and production share it is unknown. This decides whether staging test data can touch production.
  • Rollback and backups: no documented procedure, no down migrations, Supabase backup plan unknown.
  • Runtime version: no Node or Bun pin; the Node version Vercel uses is a project setting.
  • metadataBase: hardcoded to localhost in every environment; absolute metadata URLs in staging and production point at localhost. Minor, report to dev.
  • .env.example drift (HIGH for setup): the app reads NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (lib/env.ts), but the app repo's .env.example declares SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY and SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY and omits SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET. A fresh local setup from the example fails at boot. Report to the dev team.
  • Email provider: Resend as Supabase's SMTP comes only from the /qa page; it is Supabase project config, invisible in code. Confirm in the Supabase dashboard.
  • Credentials source host: the /qa page links the credentials Epic BK-29 on a jira.upexgalaxy.com host, while .agents/project.yaml names upexgalaxy72.atlassian.net and .context/project-config.md names upexgalaxy67.atlassian.net. Confirm which site holds BK-29.
  • Performance numbers: no latency, throughput or bundle budget anywhere; every performance target is [unknown] until a baseline run.
  • Supabase limits: OTP rate limit values, session lifetime and connection limits are project settings not visible in code.
  • Import time limit: whether a large Jira import finishes inside Vercel's after() window is unverified.
  • OpenAPI freshness: public/openapi.json is generated (bun run openapi:gen) and committed; not yet spot-checked against routes, and this QA repo's api/openapi-types.ts is still a stub (run bun run api:sync).
  • No figures: the diagrams capability (diagram-design skill) is not installed, so the architecture is described in tables. Install with bunx skills add https://github.com/cathrynlavery/diagram-design --skill diagram-design --yes and redraw architecture.
  • Data structure: table-level detail belongs to business-data-context, still a placeholder.
